newsitem.title: USA: Tate and Lyle unit says not target in U.S. probe.
newsitem.headline: Tate and Lyle unit says not target in U.S. probe.

text.p: A.E. Staley, a unit of Tate and Lyle Plc, said Wednesday it is not a target of an ongoing U.S. Justice Department investigation of the high fructose corn syrup market.
"We're not a target," Pat Mohan, executive vice president of A.E. Staley told Reuters.
Mohan added that A.E. Staley continues to cooperate in Justice's investigation into possible antitrust activities in high fructose corn syrup, a sweetener that is used in beverages and foods.
"We are still cooperating fully," Mohan said.

Earlier this week, Archer Daniels Midland Co pleaded guilty to two counts of price fixing in Iysine, a feed additive, and citric acid, which is used in foods, beverages and other products. ADM will pay a total of $100 million in fines.
A.E. Staley does not make lysine or citric acid.
Justice officials said this week ADM has agreed to cooperate in its ongoing investigation of high fructose corn syrup.
